## Design

### 2026-10-16 – 14 Oct: 1st Session in my The miniture roller coaster project. (Modeling the station)

**5h**

14 Oct: 1st Session in my The miniture roller coaster project. (Modeling the station)

I downloaded and installed Fusion 360 and opened a new project. The roller coaster has many repeating parts, so the best strategy is to model each part using Part Design, then assemble everything in another file.

Roller coasters in RCT have 2 main parts: the station, where guests ride and exit, and the coaster itself.

In the game, the ride is 12 x 37 grids; to make a reasonably sized miniature coaster, I set each grid to 2 cm x 2 cm. This gives the final dimensions of 24 cm x 74 cm, which isn't bad at all.

First, I decided to model the station. which is this part here:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/46e720afc8c112dd83bbf66a20eefe989487b5eb7b20a210984a32c160c22976.png)

For this, I needed dimensions, so I asked ChatGPT to give me dimensions based on some real coasters. The dimensions it gave me didn't make any sense, and i also discovered that the coaster isn't based on a real coaster like many coaster in the game, so finding any real dimensions is near impossible, meaning that i have to eyeball it or smt. so, I'll divide the station into 3 or 4 parts and model each part seperatly.

*The Station Fence*

The dimensions I chose for the fence are 0.2 mm x 0.2 mm for the post bases, and the total fence length in this image is 5 mm.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ab7ac2625b78cf994958cb8c15f22b3227ded9372e8e5ae114d80060491de239.png)

*Station Side Planks*

I made the side planks by modeling one rectangle with dimensions of 2.5 mm x 10 mm, then rounding the edges by 0.5 mm. I then extruded it by 2 mm and used the fillet tool to round the edges again.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/61209ce0b13aa8b597378a84aeaddfc7564424ced53bea2e295b328bdcfb5f69.png)

This version of the planks has many mistakes, so I created an updated version. I removed the edge rounding and fillet from every edge except the top one and set it to 0.2 mm. I also changed the dimensions to 2.5 mm x 5 mm, so both station planks will have a total width of 10 mm, leaving another 10 mm for the train.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b7c33a16d71b7399e82f6c0a7e318c5fb2ae2bd9c9debead122d04b43bb43295.png)

* Stations Rails (the part under the planks only)*

The next part I modeled was the black iron bars under the station planks. This is the sketch for the horizontal part.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/8b780272bfc12c19a99c9106bfa40c49e06622c526bd3ff2a04cd7b00804a687.png)

To create the full shape, I extruded the body by 3 mm and added a central support rod measuring 3 mm x 3 mm x 20 mm. Next, I'll add a side support
.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/fb32563c67980dc51224fb17a5dcad7a55682ca8be07fffc9e2608d22a9b8a70.png)

I spent some time changing the model a bit so it matches the one in the game. Now, the side supports.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/fe2957cb1c3fd61ba0da1d328415677d3d92fde6ecef484d7f2babb8cdfb2c85.png)

These are the dimensions for the side support,
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/a1bf9259b5349549dc92e422a87dfa2a8161fac4326f8e79ff04ca5f6653ab7c.png)

These are the dimensions for the side support.

I extruded the side supports by 1 mm and added a 1 mm chamfer to two sides. This is the final shape of the rails under the side planks. Now, the next part is the rails in the middle.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/6470b446b858c342db97285763a45b773e43a41d422a04f22ab68bba55776420.png)

I tried working on the middle, but I have no idea what those parts are, and my search led me nowhere. So, I decided to assemble the station for now. Then, I'll deal with the middle part.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/1fbbaac273ba83a76dd8aaf418a59e9bd700a858e11a00a2629f558321c95e66.png)

*Station Initial Assembly*

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/531da9bd626242c60dbd365e4fc7a5be86dfc5daa39c8c5138c833956d1dfc70.png)

This is the station after assembly. A few edits are needed: the rails under the planks need to be shorter by 2 to 3 mm, and the fence dimensions were completely wrong, so it has to be made again from scratch.

tl;dr, I started modeling the Station, I finished the sides of the station, but It needs some edits. Also the Station rails are yet to be modeled.

Total Time Spent: 5h

### 2026-10-17 – Oct 17: Modeling the Roller Coaster Station

**6h**

Oct 17: Modeling the Roller Coaster Station

Currently, I am facing a huge problem: the lack of dimensions. I scavenged every corner of the internet looking for detailed images of a real coaster, but couldn't find any. However, I just remembered that Atari released two more games after RCT 2: RCT 3 and RCT World. Looking at the wooden coaster models in both games would be a huge help.

Unfortunately, the coaster is only available in RCT 3 (a 2004 game, BTW). In my opinion, it doesn't look as good as the one in RCT 2, but it will definitely make the workflow go a lot faster.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ea190c4d9f3f28691f44dfc345912ba35831ff745611561106e4c0cff1cf9fea.png)

The past couple of hours were complete hell. The model from RCT 3 lacks the detailed railway of RCT 2, so I returned to the good old cycle of assuming, modeling, and testing, repeating it multiple times. Here are some of the issues I faced. The first one I discovered was that the planks were 22.5 mm wide instead of 20 mm. I had to model them from scratch because I hadn't set the plank width correctly from the start.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/63b799f99fbc6bf17d6fb5d66f988fe11fb6c5b387e1a0090761f9871cfa2b52.png)

The sides of the railway, of course need more remodelling. I tried modeling the part and came up with a shape that I quite liked, but, once again, I made a mistake: the shape was super thicccccc.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ede369c73d40d3b18b5a25dabb497454ac033994d314c97177d5ea9aafd440e1.png)

This is the side railway after connecting both parts.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/d925e2cc7315c9282af56bd1038c0fb26c11084e9eda3ccb637631b59eb611ae.png)

 decided to model the middle part of the railway first and return to the side part later. I modeled this part by creating a rectangle (2 × 1.5 × 10 mm), extruding it, and then filleting the edges by 0.2 mm. I did the same for the train track above (1.5 × 0.8 × 20 mm). I also added a detail to the track to make it look more like the one in the game. And this is the final shape (I hope).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/506d02802896660f12f4c1174d40135dd5067b48c1e7b4333e9dc6ec7c481cec.png)

There is still a minor issue. If you have a keen eye, or have paid any attention to this journal, you might notice that there are brakes in the middle of the track that I haven't modeled. Did I forget them? No. Will I ignore them for now? Yes.

This is the side part again after remodeling it and making a few other adjustments. This time, I won't mention the dimensions until I'm done with everything.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/22f4027224be4e8962589e02910c65aabd6ab04d2325e24df30afdb45d6962f3.png)

After some time, I joined all the parts together. There are a few minor problems that prevent the parts from fitting together very well, but I think a 0.01 mm gap won't affect the print quality, so I'll ignore it for now.

Seeing the station for the first time made me very happy. This thing took me a lot of time to make, but it was definitely worth it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/9e3aa7e6a301266fb4b75ec4f09a38d66cc76eea98316e803630bbb4a8f46a5e.png)

There's still another important part missing. Of course, it's the fence! I modeled it with dimensions of 0.4 × 2 × 6 mm and added a 0.25 mm fillet to all the edges.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/a1a617ac51c9ebe6662b64b8d7b72b05a4bc9b3f9cfeea2f36c44990057dd22f.png)

** Station Final Assembly. **

I'm super happy with how it turned out!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/44e96fba24f55a5cd3559928e2e05b7ae02bdd557c014a5fd9f08b58e0bf2584.png)

Now for the final adjustments to the station and its assembly. First, I cleaned up the edges of the fence. Before, the edges were mismatched, but now they're perfectly flush and continuous between the units. For the side parts of the rails, I adjusted the sketch dimensions. Here are the final dimensions.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/433963c80f32d252895e7960a54eef06c1682fc6c819870a7075337c907ab0d4.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/e857b00cfe5bd63685e4759512ba0586d726edfea2c55df0914318e3ff318f0d.png)

I also made many other fixes and dimension adjustments, such as reducing the middle rails from 14 mm to 12 mm.

To ensure that the station was assembled correctly, I reassembled all the parts, but this time using point-to-point movement. This ensured that the entire project was assembled correctly down to the nanometer, satisfying my OCD.

** The Final Shape of the Station Module **

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/e00c4fd6668cdfb1a00528758c71dde2bda744cb98a41c43f55cd87845a10b43.png)

TL;DR: The station model is finished!

Total time spent: 6 hours.
